prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: boundary, dispatch, authorized signals, supply/protection status; checked for health vs approved grid state); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): produces Leading Edge Tile Image; repeats pass if coverage insufficient. Blade Specialist reviews evidence. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer (temps/cooling/oil/noise checked), export cable, Export Cable Monitor (trends/alarms escalated to Control Engineer), station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on request. Substation Operator: keeps substation in limits, shift-start review, rounds, switching/isolation removal only via approved process, records actions, checks personnel access records. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling, sheds nonessential, failure→alarm; produces Start Test Trace in functional test; fuel/battery readiness checked. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped observations/alarms to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt; compared with local indications. Shore Control Room escalates hazards; retains decisions, permit status, isolation history, tests, restoration. Control Engineer: validates data (stale→unverified), investigates discrepancies before remote reliance, reviews restored state. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): ranks work via Squall Window Bulletin; produces Deferred Task Rationale. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; permit submission, revised windows coordinated, closes authorization. Crew Transfer Vessel uses Harness Audit Card. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) uses Position Quality Flag. Grid Dispatcher: safety>protection>export. Marine Coordinator; Vessel Master accepts/pauses/aborts. Weather Analyst uses Wave Burst Record. Port Agent issues Berth Slot Confirmation. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release until reviews/isolations complete; Work Permit Portal checked for current authorizations. HSE Officer confirms controls. Field Supervisor: starts only with

New part:
S355: Foxglove is exercised under the approved test procedure to confirm reliable backup starting and stable output.
S356: The operator records test results and raises a defect promptly if the Emergency Generator fails to start or sustain its required load.
S357: The Cybersecurity Gateway uses the revocation receipt to support access control during routine account and session reviews.
S358: Switching is performed only by authorized personnel using approved instructions and positive confirmation of equipment identity.
S359: Before operating a breaker or isolator, the operator verifies the required clearances and confirms that affected parties are informed.
S360: If a protection alarm, abnormal electrical condition, or loss of critical monitoring occurs, the operator limits further switching and escalates the condition.
S361: The operator places the Offshore Substation in Substation Degraded when required by operating procedures and communicates the resulting restrictions.
S362: The Grid Dispatcher is notified when a condition could affect export capability or compliance with grid instructions.
S363: The Electrical Technician supports fault diagnosis and maintenance under the applicable work authorization and isolation controls.
S364: The Shore Control Room receives concise status updates, including operating limitations and the expected time of the next review.
S365: Shift records capture inspections, alarms, tests, switching actions, defects, and handover items so that decisions remain traceable.
S366: Grid export is coordinated against the dispatch instructions, equipment capability, and the agreed operating limits for the connection.
S367: Grid Dispatcher issues active-power targets and ramp instructions through the established dispatch channel.
S368: Control Engineer reviews each instruction for consistency with current plant status before applying it.
S369: SCADA Gateway provides the operational measurements used to track delivered power and instruction response.
S370: Fleet Dispatch Console compares the requested output with available turbine capability and known operating restrictions.
S371: The Shore Control Room maintains the current dispatch target, ramp rate, and next review time in the shift record.
S372: Grid Interface Relay produces an Export Limit Advisory when available export capability falls below the active dispatch target.
S373: Wildmere applies the accepted export ceiling to control outputs and records its effective time for audit.
S374: Shore Control Room uses the tap snapshot to check the recorded transformer position during export reviews.
S375: Control Engineer confirms that the control response follows the instruction and remains within the permitted ramp rate.
S376: When a Grid Constraint is active, the operator records its scope, start time, and expected review point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
